title: Eager-QK fuse + rotary normalization fast-path and streaming-KV micro-scheduler
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Small-batch, low-concurrency inference workloads (PLG webhooks, customer assistants, SDK local tests) spend disproportionate time in QK preparation and rotary normalization. Existing FlashAttention variants provide excellent throughput at high batch sizes but miss a low-latency fast-path for eager QK fusion + device-side rotary normalization while streaming KV micro-batches. This PR introduces an alternative fast-path designed to reduce per-request token latency and cost for 1-8 request micro-batches while preserving compatibility with our continuous batching and KV caching stack.

What this PR does (high-level): Adds an "eager QK fuse" kernel that fuses pre-softmax QK matmuls, rotary application, and small-size softmax into a single GPU kernel for short sequences; introduces a device-side rotary-normalization helper to eliminate a host-side normalizer roundtrip; implements a streaming-KV micro-scheduler that pipeline-evicts and re-inserts small KV chunks to keep GPU memory pressure low while preserving prefix cache hits; and exposes a runtime flag to enable the small-batch fast-path (off by default).

Design notes: The eager QK kernel is optimized for typical interactive sequence lengths (<=128) and request micro-batch sizes (1..8). It avoids large temporary allocations by writing QK and rotary outputs directly into shared/global memory pages suitable for the fused softmax. The micro-scheduler allows the runtime to (a) detect small-batch latency-sensitive flows, (b) allocate a limited number of fast-path slots per GPU, and (c) progressively fall back to the standard FlashAttention path when contention rises. The implementation is backward-compatible: the canonical KV cache layout and the public inference API remain unchanged; the kernel is selected at scheduling time.

Compatibility and safety: Feature gated behind runtime config `enable_eager_qk_fastpath` (cluster and per-model override). We add conservative checks for sequence length, dtype (fp16/nbits8 supported), and KV layout. The code contains a disabled-but-available emulation path for CI that runs on CPU to validate numerical equivalence on small examples.

Performance summary (microbenchmarks, internal): For a 1-4 request micro-batch with seq_len=64 on A100-80GB: median tail latency reduced by 18% (single-token step) and 22% p50 for generation with small prompt prefixes; aggregate token throughput improves 7-12% on these small-batch regimes. For larger batches (>=32) there is no regression — scheduler prefers FlashAttention path. End-to-end e2e tests showed negligible output diffs (max rel error < 1e-4 for fp16 baseline).

Files changed (high-level): runtime/attention/eager_qk_kernel.cu, runtime/attention/kernels.h, runtime/scheduler/micro_scheduler.cc, runtime/kv/streaming_eviction.cc, tests/attention/eager_qk_unittests.cpp, bench/bench_eager_qk.py, docs/runtime/fastpath.md

Rollout plan: Merge to main, run a 48-hour canary on dedicated pools with the feature enabled for a soft percentage of small-batch traffic (10%). If metrics (latency p95/p99, error rates) remain stable we will enable the fast-path by default for model tiers marked as latency-sensitive.

Related: ENG-4879 (small-batch perf initiative), ENG-4921 (KV cache streaming), internal benchmark RFC 2026/02.

Checklist:
- [x] unit tests for kernel logic (CPU emulation)
- [x] integration test with KV cache on small-batch workloads
- [x] bench scripts for repeatable measurement
- [x] runtime flag and config docs

Notes: There is a follow-up to add an autotuner for slot counts and a telemetry histogram to expose fast-path hit-rate per-model (tracked in a separate PR).

release_notes: Adds an optional low-latency fast-path that fuses QK + rotary + softmax for short sequences and small micro-batches. Improves latency for interactive small-batch workloads. Feature is gated behind runtime flag `enable_eager_qk_fastpath`.
